architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed pyzbar dependency and upgraded zxing-cpp to version 3.0.0, eliminating the need for custom wheel builds
architecture_decisions.rationale: pyzbar was unmaintained (last release March 2022) and relied on libzbar which hadn't been updated in 16 years. zxing-cpp 3.0.0 now provides pre-built wheels for all supported architectures, simplifying dependency management and removing the need for custom builds.
alternatives_considered: Keeping both libraries with pyzbar as fallback
Maintaining custom wheel builds for zxing-cpp
Switching to a different barcode library entirely

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed libzbar0 system package from all Docker and CI configurations
architecture_decisions.rationale: Since pyzbar is no longer used, its underlying system dependency libzbar0 is no longer required. This reduces container size and simplifies installation requirements across all deployment scenarios.
alternatives_considered: Keeping libzbar0 for potential future compatibility
Making libzbar0 optional with conditional installation

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed CONSUMER_BARCODE_SCANNER setting and associated validation logic
architecture_decisions.rationale: With only one barcode reader backend (zxing-cpp), the configuration option becomes unnecessary. This eliminates conditional code paths, reduces complexity, and prevents user confusion about which scanner to choose.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the setting as a no-op for backward compatibility
Deprecating the setting first before removal
Making the setting read-only with a fixed value

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed pyzbar-specific code and consolidated to use only zxing-cpp in barcode detection logic
architecture_decisions.rationale: Eliminated conditional branching based on scanner type, simplified the detect() method by directly calling read_barcodes_zxing(), and removed the now-unused reader function selection logic. This makes the code more maintainable and reduces cognitive load.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the pyzbar code as commented-out reference
Creating an abstract barcode reader interface
Moving pyzbar code to a separate module for potential future use

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed pyzbar-specific test classes and consolidated test coverage around zxing-cpp
architecture_decisions.rationale: Eliminated duplicate test classes (TestBarcodeZxing, TestAsnBarcodesZxing) that were created to test both backends. Updated remaining tests to reflect that zxing-cpp now detects barcodes that pyzbar couldn't detect (like small QR codes without upscaling).
alternatives_considered: Keeping pyzbar tests as historical reference
Creating generic tests that work with any backend
Maintaining separate test suites for regression testing

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated all documentation to reflect the removal of pyzbar and the CONSUMER_BARCODE_SCANNER setting
architecture_decisions.rationale: Provided clear migration guidance in docs/migration.md, removed references to pyzbar from configuration documentation, and updated installation instructions to exclude libzbar0. This ensures users understand the change and know what actions to take.
alternatives_considered: Keeping old documentation for historical reference
Creating a separate migration document
Only documenting the change in release notes

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated Python version and uv version in CI workflows and cleaned up mypy baseline
architecture_decisions.rationale: While removing barcode support, also updated tooling versions to stay current. Removed mypy errors related to pyzbar imports that are no longer relevant, keeping the type checking baseline clean.
alternatives_considered: Making tooling updates in a separate PR
Keeping old Python/uv versions for stability
Ignoring mypy errors instead of removing them

implementation_summary:
The implementation removes legacy barcode reader support by consolidating all barcode functionality to use zxing-cpp exclusively. This was a strategic decision to simplify the codebase, reduce maintenance burden, and improve barcode detection reliability.

The key approach was systematic removal: starting with dependencies (removing pyzbar from pyproject.toml and libzbar0 from system packages), then configuration (removing the CONSUMER_BARCODE_SCANNER setting), followed by code refactoring (eliminating conditional logic in barcodes.py), and finally updating tests and documentation. The migration was made seamless by ensuring zxing-cpp supports all the same barcode formats as pyzbar while providing better detection capabilities.

An important pattern in this change is the comprehensive nature of the removal - not just deleting code but also updating CI configurations, documentation, type checking baselines, and dependency files. The implementation maintains backward compatibility in functionality while simplifying the user experience by removing configuration options. The documentation updates in docs/migration.md provide clear guidance for users, explaining the rationale and required actions, which is crucial for a breaking change like this.
